coverage_notes: Exhaustive sweep across foundational scholarly literature on graph visualization aesthetics and readability. Coverage spans: (1) seminal textbooks and handbooks (Tollis/Di Battista, Tamassia, Munzner); (2) core aesthetic criteria research (crossing minimization, symmetry, edge density, bend minimization, area efficiency—with Purchase's formal metrics); (3) foundational algorithmic work (Eades spring-electric model, Fruchterman-Reingold, Kobourov force-directed methods, Sugiyama hierarchical layout); (4) cognitive-load empirical studies (Huang-Eades-Hong effectiveness model; Purchase user studies validating crossing importance); (5) major layout families (orthogonal/planar, circular, hierarchical, edge-bundling, proximity drawings); (6) modern research angles (dynamic graphs, 3D/VR visualization, large-scale LOD, node-link vs matrix tradeoffs, Gestalt principles, community detection); (7) visual perception foundations (Cleveland-McGill encoding hierarchy, visual encoding channels, perceptual grouping); (8) systems/tools (Graphviz/neato stress majorization, OGDF, yFiles). Deduplication applied (e.g., Huang et al. paper appears in multiple contexts, counted once). Named authorities: Huang, Kobourov, Eades, Tufte, Munzner, Shneiderman, Norman, Pirolli, Purchase, Di Battista, Tamassia, Tollis. Notable gap: specific UIST/CHI proceedings papers (searched; found references but URLs often point to ACM DL abstracts requiring institutional access—marked reference-only). Breadth: 30+ sources across T0-T3 tiers, primarily open-access arXiv and institutional PDFs, some paywalled reference material.

sources.title: Handbook of Graph Drawing and Visualization
sources.notes: Comprehensive handbook edited by Roberto Tamassia, seminal reference covering topological/geometric foundations, layout algorithms (trees, planar, orthogonal, circular, hierarchical, 3D), systems, and applications. Foundational for understanding aesthetic criteria and algorithm families.

sources.title: Graph Drawing: Algorithms for the Visualization of Graphs
sources.notes: Tollis, Di Battista, Eades, Tamassia (1999); foundational textbook covering fundamental algorithmic techniques and aesthetic principles for graph drawing.

sources.title: Visualization Analysis and Design
sources.notes: Tamara Munzner's comprehensive framework for visualization design and analysis; covers graph drawing as key technique-driven interest; establishes methodology for design space analysis.

sources.title: The Visual Display of Quantitative Information
sources.notes: Edward Tufte (1983, 2nd ed. 2001); foundational principles for graphical excellence, graphical integrity, data-ink ratio, and minimizing chartjunk—direct application to graph aesthetics.

sources.title: Measuring Effectiveness of Graph Visualizations: A Cognitive Load Perspective
sources.notes: Weidong Huang, Peter Eades, Seok-Hee Hong (2009); seminal cognitive load study proposing model of task performance, mental effort, and cognitive load; introduces visualization efficiency metric combining performance and mental effort.

sources.title: Metrics for Graph Drawing Aesthetics
sources.notes: Helen Purchase (2002); foundational work formalizing metrics for seven aesthetic criteria (symmetry, edge crossings, bends, etc.); continuous metrics (0-1 scale) for assessing aesthetic conformance.

sources.title: Graph Drawing Aesthetics—Created by Users, Not Algorithms
sources.notes: Helen Purchase et al.; empirical user studies validating relative importance of aesthetic criteria; demonstrated edge crossing minimization overwhelmingly important for task performance.

sources.title: Towards Faithful Graph Visualizations
sources.notes: arXiv paper on faithfulness metrics for large graphs and crossing minimization; addresses readability of complex visualizations.

sources.title: Confluent Drawings: Visualizing Non-planar Diagrams in a Planar Way
sources.notes: Approach to reduce visual clutter and crossing issues in non-planar graphs through bundled edge routing.

sources.title: A Quality Metric for Visualization of Clusters in Graphs
sources.notes: Proposes metrics for evaluating cluster visualization quality, relevant to aesthetic evaluation frameworks.

sources.title: Improving Graph Drawing Readability by Incorporating Readability Metrics: A Software Tool for Network Analysts
sources.notes: Dunne & Shneiderman; practical tool implementing readability metrics to guide layout optimization decisions.

sources.title: Exploring the Limits of Complexity: A Survey of Empirical Studies on Graph Visualisation
sources.notes: Comprehensive survey of empirical user studies evaluating graph visualizations; meta-analysis of aesthetic criteria effects across tasks and graph sizes.

sources.title: Spring Embedders and Force Directed Graph Drawing Algorithms
sources.notes: Comprehensive survey of force-directed methods from Eades (1984) through modern variants; covers spring-electric model, repulsive/attractive forces, and stress majorization.

sources.title: Force-Directed Drawing Algorithms
sources.notes: Stephen Kobourov chapter in Handbook of Graph Drawing; authoritative on force-directed methods, aesthetics goals (uniform edge lengths, symmetry, even vertex distribution).

sources.title: Graph Drawing by Force-Directed Placement
sources.notes: Fruchterman & Reingold (1991); foundational force-directed algorithm improving on Eades with even vertex distribution; major aesthetic goals: symmetry, uniform edge lengths, distribution.

sources.title: Layered Graph Drawing (Sugiyama)
sources.notes: Overview of Sugiyama hierarchical layout algorithm; key aesthetic goals: minimize upward edges, uniform layer distribution, minimize edge spans, minimize crossings.

sources.title: New Quality Metrics for Dynamic Graph Drawing
sources.notes: Metrics for evaluating dynamic graph drawings; addresses stability, readability, and aesthetic conformance under temporal changes.

sources.title: Visual Stability in Dynamic Graph Drawings
sources.notes: Formal model for quantifying visual stability in dynamic drawings; addresses mental map preservation and cognitive impact of layout changes.

sources.title: A Sparse Stress Model
sources.notes: Stress minimization via multidimensional scaling (MDS); reduces computation while preserving distance-based aesthetic quality.

sources.title: Graphviz Neato Layout Algorithm
sources.notes: Production system implementing stress majorization for undirected graphs; practical application of MDS-based layout minimizing stress function.

sources.title: A Survey on Graph Drawing Beyond Planarity
sources.notes: Comprehensive survey covering planar, upward, orthogonal, and quasi-planar drawings; aesthetic criteria and computational complexity.

sources.title: Upward Planar Drawing
sources.notes: Upward planar drawing for directed acyclic graphs; monotonic upward edges maintain hierarchy and readability.

sources.title: Orthogonal Layout with Optimal Face Complexity
sources.notes: Kobourov et al.; orthogonal drawings with optimization of bends and face complexity; addresses readability via geometric constraints.

sources.title: Hierarchical Edge Bundling: Visualization of Adjacency Relations in Hierarchical Data
sources.notes: Holten (2006); foundational edge bundling technique reducing visual clutter; bundles edges along hierarchy paths for improved readability.

sources.title: Edge-Path Bundling: A Less Ambiguous Edge Bundling Approach
sources.notes: Recent advance in edge bundling addressing ambiguity; improves readability for dense graphs while maintaining traceability.

sources.title: Towards Intelligible Graph Data Visualization Using Circular Layout
sources.notes: Circular layout cognitive benefits; supports perceptual grouping and cluster identification through symmetric radial arrangement.

sources.title: Proximity Drawings
sources.notes: Chapter on Gabriel, Delaunay, and other proximity graph classes; aesthetic criterion: adjacency implies spatial proximity.

sources.title: Revisited Experimental Comparison of Node-Link and Matrix Representations
sources.notes: Comprehensive empirical study comparing node-link diagrams vs adjacency matrices; finds task-dependent tradeoffs in readability.

sources.title: CHORDination: Evaluating Visual Design Choices in Chord Diagrams for Network Data
sources.notes: Evaluates design choices (layout, color, line width) in chord diagrams; empirical study of readability and aesthetic preferences.

sources.title: Gestalt Principles in Graph Drawing
sources.notes: Application of Gestalt principles (proximity, similarity, closure, continuity) to improve readability through perceptual organization.

sources.title: Visual Encoding: Principles and Effectiveness
sources.notes: Foundations of visual encoding channels (position, color, size, shape); Cleveland-McGill effectiveness hierarchy; applies to graph node/edge visual variables.

sources.title: Perceptual and Cognitive Foundations of Information Visualization
sources.notes: Review of perceptual and cognitive science underlying visualization design; preattentive processing, visual attention, memory; applies to graph readability.

sources.title: Rational Analyses of Information Foraging on the Web
sources.notes: Peter Pirolli; foundational theory of information scent and navigation; applies to visual cue design for graph exploration.

sources.title: Visual Network Analysis in Immersive Environments: A Survey
sources.notes: Recent survey of graph visualization in VR/AR; depth perception, stereoscopy, spatial cognition; emerging dimension of readability.

sources.title: The VRNetzer Platform Enables Interactive Network Analysis in Virtual Reality
sources.notes: Production VR system for network visualization; demonstrates immersive 3D as alternative to 2D aesthetics; improved speed for large network comprehension.

sources.title: Bend Minimization
sources.notes: Overview of polyline edge aesthetic; minimizing bends a key criterion alongside crossing; orthogonal/rectilinear drawings emphasized.

sources.title: Community Detection and Visualization in Social Networks: Integrating Structural and Semantic Information
sources.notes: Integration of community structure with layout aesthetics; improved readability via clustering and hierarchical visualization.

sources.title: An LOD Model for Graph Visualization and Its Application in Web Navigation
sources.notes: Level-of-detail strategies for large graphs; progressive simplification preserving readability at multiple zoom scales.

sources.title: The Multi-Dimensional Landscape of Graph Drawing Metrics
sources.notes: Recent comprehensive overview of aesthetic and readability metrics; synthesis of formal measures for evaluating layout quality.

sources.title: Proceedings of the 31st International Symposium on Graph Drawing and Network Visualization (GD 2023)
sources.notes: Recent conference proceedings capturing state-of-art in graph drawing; peer-reviewed papers on algorithms, aesthetics, and applications.

sources.title: Algorithms for Drawing Graphs: an Annotated Bibliography
sources.notes: Di Battista, Eades, Tamassia, Tollis (1994); foundational annotated bibliography covering aesthetic criteria and algorithm families.

sources.title: An Eye Tracking Study into the Effects of Graph Layout
sources.notes: Empirical eye-tracking study measuring cognitive effort and attention patterns in response to layout aesthetics; validates importance of crossing minimization.
